set.body:
Phase: core. Track: engine.

Outcome
A download or a directory page costs what the caller's own scope requires, however large the installation grows.

Why
The 18 November audit reads the code as rechecking authority every 64 KiB by reloading principals, releases, datasets, grants and organization records. That is 16,384 checks for a 1 GiB file. It also reads each directory page as loading a whole organization snapshot. CORE3 measures both.

Acceptance
1. Authority checks during delivery, and directory reads, use scoped, indexed reads. Decisions match the pure policy evaluator on fixed grants, dataset scope, membership, expiry, disabled sessions and lifecycle state.
2. Query plans and row counts show that a chunk check no longer reads installation-wide state and that a page does not materialize all organization history.
3. Revoking or expiring permission during a long transfer still stops the next chunk.
4. CORE3's budgets are met at both population sizes. Content hashes and upgrade compatibility are unchanged.
5. If CORE3 shows the budgets are already met with room to spare, close this item with that evidence instead.

Start from (line references from the audit at b82cd14)
- modules/application/src/main/scala/sanctity/application/NativeRepository.scala line 122.
- modules/postgres/src/main/scala/sanctity/postgres/PostgresCatalog.scala line 563, and PolicySql.scala line 40.
- modules/postgres/src/main/scala/sanctity/postgres/PostgresOrganizationCatalog.scala line 282.

Evidence
Before and after numbers on the same workload, and the comparison with the pure evaluator.
set.title: CORE4: Authority and directory reads follow the caller's scope (was OPS02)
